what_changed: FCC announces April 11, 2025 as the effective date of the TCPA consent-revocation rules in FCC 24-24 (89 FR 15756), after OMB approved the information collections on September 26, 2024. Per the eCFR diff: new 47 CFR 64.1200(a)(10) lets a called party revoke prior express consent (including prior express written consent) for calls and texts under 64.1200(a)(1)-(3) and (c)(2) by any reasonable method; an automated voice or key-press opt-out, a reply text of 'stop', 'quit', 'end', 'revoke', 'opt out', 'cancel' or 'unsubscribe', or a caller-designated website or number is per se reasonable; other reply wording counts if a reasonable person would read it as revocation; one-way text protocols must disclose that and give alternative opt-out means on each text; revocations must be honored within a reasonable time not exceeding ten business days; callers may not designate an exclusive revocation channel. New 64.1200(a)(11): other means (e.g., voicemail or email) create a rebuttable presumption of revocation. 64.1200(a)(9)(i)(F) (package delivery opt-outs) moves from 30 days to six business days and 64.1200(d)(3) (do-not-call requests) from 30 days to ten business days.
compliant_agent_must_now: From April 11, 2025, any caller or texter using an autodialer or an artificial or prerecorded voice (including an AI voice agent), first-party or third-party: (1) treat any reasonable expression of 'don't contact me' as a revocation, including the listed keywords and free-text replies a reasonable person would read as revocation, spoken requests during calls, and requests by voicemail or email (rebuttable presumption); (2) stop the robocalls/robotexts covered by 64.1200(a)(1)-(3) and (c)(2) within ten business days of receipt at most; (3) never require a specific channel to revoke; (4) if texts are sent on a no-reply protocol, state that on each text and give alternative opt-out means; (5) send at most one confirmation text, without marketing, preferably within five minutes (64.1200(a)(12)).
open_questions_for_deploying_team: How quickly does a revocation captured by the AI agent (spoken or text) propagate to every dialer, texting platform and vendor acting for the lender? Is it within ten business days, and is the target shorter?

Does the deployment treat a revocation in response to one type of message (e.g., payment reminder) as covering other robocalls or robotexts from the same lender? The FCC order's scope on that point is not stated in this notice and should be checked.
Do state rows (e.g., FL, MA) or Regulation F (REGF-MEDIA-001) impose stricter or different opt-out handling for the same contacts?
rationale: The notice gives the effective date; the operative text comes from the eCFR diff of 64.1200 (2025-04-10 to 2025-04-11). Stage A's 'six business days' was the package-delivery provision; the general revocation period is ten business days. Stage B: read SUMMARY, DATES, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION and any regulatory text from the saved GovInfo full text (389 of 389 words).
